AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Project-level instructions for AI coding agents working on this repository. This file records only what the code, DESCRIPTION, Makefile, and the function documentation do not already tell you.

Package overview

ggstatsplot creates ggplot2 plots with statistical details in the plot. It is a visualization frontend for statsExpressions: statistical computation belongs there, and plotting functions here should delegate to it rather than duplicate statistical logic.

grouped_* variants map the corresponding plotting function across a grouping variable and combine the plots with patchwork; follow the existing purrr and patchwork::wrap_plots() pattern. ggcoefstats() has no grouped variant.

Validation gate

The repository prompts and skills refer to this as the full validation gate:

air format . --check
make lint
make hooks
make check
git diff --check

If Air reports drift, run air format . and inspect the result. Run the narrowest relevant test file first, for example Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local(filter = "ggbetweenstats")'. make document only renders README.Rmd; it does not regenerate roxygen output.

Versioning and changelog

  • Development versions use a fourth-component .9000 suffix.
  • Keep the version in DESCRIPTION, codemeta.json, and the first NEWS.md heading synchronized.
  • Record user-facing compatibility or behavior changes in NEWS.md; omit routine dependency, formatting, lint, test, CI, and generated-file maintenance.

Testing

  • tests/testthat.R runs tests only on Linux and macOS, so there are no Windows snapshot variants.
  • Codecov requires 100% project and patch coverage.
  • Set seeds before tests that use random or Bayesian computations. Suppress warnings only when a test intentionally exercises a warning-producing path.
  • Plot output is covered by vdiffr snapshots (expect_doppelganger()) in tests/testthat/_snaps/. A few use variant = for platform (darwin/, linux/) or R-version (r-4.7/) differences; add a variant only when the difference is confirmed to be renderer-specific.
  • Treat broad snapshot diffs after dependency updates as likely renderer churn. Compare the old and new dependency builds under the same R and graphics stack; if both reproduce the same SVG changes, restore the repository snapshots rather than committing them. Confirm legitimate baseline updates against the snapshot artifact the R-CMD-check workflow uploads on failure.

Code conventions

  • Use the base R pipe (|>), not %>%, and snake_case names.
  • Use @autoglobal from roxyglobals where appropriate.

Roxygen documentation

  • After changing roxygen comments, run Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()' and commit the generated NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd, API (from pkgapi), and R/globals.R (from roxyglobals). Do not edit generated files by hand.
  • pkgapi is not on CRAN; install it with pak::pak("r-lib/pkgapi").
  • Regenerate with the roxygen2 release in Config/roxygen2/version. A newer release rewrites that field and may reformat NAMESPACE; bump it only deliberately, together with the regenerated output.
  • Several parameters are inherited from statsExpressions via @inheritParams, so generated .Rd text depends on the installed version. Regenerate against the version DESCRIPTION requires (its GitHub development version while listed under Remotes, otherwise its CRAN release).
  • Shared documentation lives in fragments; edit the fragment, not the generated output. man/rmd-fragments/*.Rmd are pulled into function docs with roxygen child= chunks and into vignettes/web_only/ articles with asis file chunks. man/md-fragments/*.md are included by vignettes with asis file chunks. In articles, use asis file chunks rather than child=: pkgdown renders them from a temporary file, so relative child paths do not resolve.

Repository skills and prompts

Task-specific procedures live in .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Read one only when the task matches it:

  • create-release: prepare, submit, resume, or publish a CRAN release.
  • update-dependencies: update dependencies, change the minimum R version, or add, remove, or move a dependency.
  • maintain-ci: change or debug workflows under .github/workflows/.

User-invoked prompts (address-review.md and simplify-codebase.md) live in .github/prompts/. Keep each topic in exactly one place: this file for every-session rules, a skill or prompt for task-specific procedures.

Continuous integration

Workflows under .github/workflows/ are thin callers of shared reusable workflows; the maintain-ci skill covers changing them.

  • Reference IndrajeetPatil/workflows reusable workflows as @main, never a commit SHA. The owner maintains them and is the only person who can contribute to this repository, so there is no external-contributor risk, and @main keeps it on the latest version. Code scanners (CodeQL actions/unpinned-tag, zizmor unpinned-uses) flag this by design: do not report it or propose a pin; dismiss such alerts as “won’t fix” with this reason.

Benchmarks

See benchmarks/README.md for API coverage policy, workload catalogue, local execution, and interpretation of CodSpeed results.

Pull requests

Open pull requests as ready for review. After pushing, wait for CI and fix any failures, then get Codex approval on the current head before squash-merging.
